decisive_item.title: Nvidia GPU Debt Backstop Unleashes the AI Project Trinity: Capital, Offtake and Datacenters
decisive_item.who: Sharon AI (counterparty disclosure, reported by SemiAnalysis)
decisive_item.passage: Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B

meaning.what: total value of NVIDIA's backstop on Sharon's 72MW Australian AI factory (up to 40,000 GB300)

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis says market estimates for Nvidia shipment volumes and revenue in the second half of 2026 are materially below its supply-chain-tracking estimates.
passages: Nvidia revenue is skyrocketing, and even 3 years into the build out, the general market is still materially lower on shipment volumes and revenue estimates for Nvidia in the 2nd half of this year versus our through supply chain tracking in the Accelerator Model .

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis forecasts annual AI capital spending will exceed $2 trillion in calendar 2028 and cumulative spending will reach about $11.1 trillion over 2024–2029, with credit markets the main funding source.
passages: Annual AI Capex – including GPUs, networking, storage and attached CPU compute as well as for the Datacenters to house AI compute – will be well north of $2T in 2028. Cumulative AI Capex from 2024 to 2029 will reach ~$11.1T, and credit markets will be the main funding source for this buildout.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis says data-center supply improved by early 2026, chip production became the limiting constraint, and financing was a significant obstacle to expanding compute by mid-2026.
passages: In 2025, we wrote extensively about how datacenter capacity was the bottleneck for AI compute growth. By early 2026, the datacenter supply situation improved considerably, but it became clear that chip production was now the limiting constraint. Now – mid-way through the year – it is clear that financing will now be one of the most significant obstacles to ramping large scale compute broadly available to everyone.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reports that Nvidia has started providing Neoclouds take-or-pay minimum-revenue guarantees on GPU capacity in exchange for a share of revenue above the guaranteed level.
passages: This is why Nvidia has stepped in and has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes themselves . In the backstop program, Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment to Neoclouds – a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity. In exchange for this backstop, Nvidia also shares in a portion of the Neocloud’s revenue earned above the backstop level.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reports that Nvidia has started backstopping Neoclouds’ data-center leases.
passages: Here, Nvidia is diving even deeper, as it has started backstopping datacenter leases.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis says Nvidia’s backstop program typically runs for six years, with Nvidia ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed prices that vary over the term.
passages: Nvidia’s backstop program is typically six years in length, and during these six years, Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over the time period.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis models an illustrative Nvidia backstop price averaging $2.36 over six years, which it considers near the low end of the range, and expects most Neoclouds to negotiate higher backstops.
passages: The below table is an illustrative example to explain the basic terms of the program – we present a backstop pricing curve that we believe to be on the lower end of the backstop range – in this case at an average of $2.36 over the six-year period, but we expect that most Neoclouds will negotiate higher backstops.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SharonAI’s June 2026 Australia AI-factory deal includes a six-year backstop for up to 40,000 GB300 GPUs valued at $4.88 billion; SharonAI plans a 132 MW footprint, 102 MW contracted, and more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs by mid-2027.
passages: The first is SharonAI’s 72MW AI factory in Australia. Announced in June 2026, the deal has SharonAI scaling up to as many as 40,000 GB300s under a six-year backstop. Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B, which works out to an implied floor of about $2.33/hr/GPU on average over the six year period. Sharon AI’s footprint is now set to grow to 132MW with 102MW contracted, and the company guides to reaching more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs in total (inclusive of the 40,000 GB300s backstopped) by mid-2027.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Firmus announced a 360 MW AI cluster in Batam, Indonesia, with an Nvidia backstop on June 29, 2026; it is likely to be housed at a DayOne facility in Kabil Industrial Tech Park.
passages: Firmus’s 360MW AI Cluster in Batam, Indonesia is the next major project announced with an Nvidia backstop. It will likely be housed in a DayOne facility in Kabil Industrial Tech Park (KITP). Announced just recently on June 29 th , 2026, this project shows the scale at which Nvidia is rolling out the backstop program.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Firmus expects $25 billion to $30 billion of customer revenue over six years from its project; SemiAnalysis expects Firmus to share some revenue above the backstop level with Nvidia.
passages: Firmus announced that they expect $25B to $30B of customer revenue over the six years. We expect a portion of the revenue above the backstop level will be shared with Nvidia as per the structure we outlined earlier today.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Firmus announced a 600 MW firm-energy deal with Gunvor that will underwrite 1.2 GW of renewable development and 1.5 GWh of storage in South Australia by 2032.
passages: Beyond this – Firmus also announced a 600MW firm-energy deal with Gunvor that will also underwrite 1.2GW of new renewables development and 1.5GWh of storage in South Australia by 2032.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis says other Neoclouds have Nvidia backstops, although many have not been publicly disclosed.
passages: We have seen many other neoclouds having backstops, but many are not public yet.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis estimates initial lending for Nvidia-backstopped Neocloud projects will price wider than five-year hyperscale-backed deals at about SOFR plus 225 basis points and 5.9% yield, but tighter than CoreWeave’s five-year unsecured bonds at about 10% yield.
passages: We think that initial lending will be at a wider spread than the current 5y backstopped hyperscale deals which come in at around SOFR + 225bps (roughly equivalent to a Z-spread of 195bps, or about 5.9% total yield) but at a tighter spread than CoreWeave’s 5-year unsecured corporate bond which has a yield of ~10% (roughly equivalent to Z-spread of 600bps).
